cohort: 12 virgin female Wistar rats were divided into two groups: a control group (n=6) fed a standard diet, and an experimental group (n=6) fed a high-fat, high-cholesterol diet for 6 weeks prior to and throughout pregnancy.
finding: Maternal obesity induced by an HFHC diet in rats significantly increased intrauterine pressure by 1.5-fold and frequency of contractions by fivefold, and prolonged labor duration by 9 hours compared to controls.
